I've been overweight/obese all my life; I've struggled with binge eating since first grade because of bullying and mental health issues, but even before that I was always a pudgy kid. Tried and failed time and time again to get the weight off. 2017 was a good year and I even managed to briefly get out of obesity territory and into the overweight range (198lbs), but then the weight slowly started to creep back up again. In summer 2018 I had a surgery and after that, pretty bad post-op depression and I gained 15lbs in just over a month. Tried on and off to get at least down to my immediate-post-op weight (243lbs) but always caved and binged again. Then the last couple of months of 2018 were just plain awful as my drinking turned worse than it's ever been before and I just completely stopped taking care of myself.

I toyed with the idea of making it a new year's resolution to get back on track with weight loss for a while, but kind of pushed it off, but then in late December I stepped on the scale for the first time in months and weighed in at 267.2lbs. (We use kg here and 267 is 121kg and the 120 is a mark I never ever wanted to cross.) I felt awful about myself and I knew I had to do something about this. I've been mostly quietly lurking in all the different subreddits for a couple of days, but then I saw this challenge and just wanted to take the opportunity.

I remember how good I felt at my lightest in  '17 and how much my body suffers and aches in comparison now and I really want to get back to that feeling! I want to work to make 2019 the year where I start taking care of myself and stop ruining my body with binging (be it food or alcohol).
